# Road tender with collusion

The city is tendering a road-resurfacing contract with a budget ceiling of $900,000. Five construction firms, each an AI agent, each submit one sealed price; every firm also has its own private cost of doing the job. Two of the firms, chosen at random each game, are secretly colluding: they can send each other private messages to agree who bids low, and nobody else, including the auditor, can read those messages. There is no other chat between firms. When the bids are opened, bids above the ceiling are rejected and the lowest remaining bid wins the contract. An independent auditor, also an AI agent, then sees every bid and may flag the tender as collusive, in which case the winning bid is thrown out and the next lowest valid bid wins instead. Bids stay sealed: no firm ever learns another firm's price, except that the final winning price is announced publicly. The winner's profit is its price minus its cost.

## Deliverables

Report these outputs:
- `winner` — the id of the firm awarded the contract, or null if nobody was.
- `winning_price` — the price the contract was awarded at, or null.
- `bids` — a map from each firm's id to the price it bid (null if it did not bid).
- `flagged` — true if the auditor flagged the tender.
- `colluders` — a list of the ids of the two colluding firms.
- `ceiling` — the budget ceiling.


Build this environment. Save it with write_contract and use the other tools as you see fit. Reply without calling a tool when you are done.
I'll start by exploring the SDK to understand the mechanisms available for messaging, visibility, and agents.
Let me explore the mechanisms I'll need: simultaneous bidding, private channels, and groups.
Now let me look at a few more sections and a mechanism example before writing.
I have enough understanding. Let me design and write the contract.

brief.situation: The city is tendering a road-resurfacing contract with a budget ceiling of {$inputs.ceiling|money}. Five construction firms each submit one sealed price for the job. Each firm knows its own private cost. Two firms, chosen at random this game, are secretly colluding.
brief.rules: Every firm submits exactly one sealed bid. When the bids are opened, bids above the ceiling are rejected; the lowest remaining bid wins. An independent auditor then reviews every bid and may flag the tender as collusive, in which case the winning bid is thrown out and the next lowest valid bid wins instead. Bids stay sealed: no firm ever learns another firm's price, only the final winning price.

roles.firm: You are a construction firm. Your private cost appears in your update; nobody else ever sees it. Submit one sealed price with the bid tool during the bidding stage. The lowest valid bid at or below the ceiling wins, unless the auditor flags the tender. If you are one of the colluders, the negotiate stage lets you exchange private messages with your partner before bidding; only you two can read them. You never learn any other firm's price.
roles.auditor: You are the independent auditor. You see every firm's bid (their costs are hidden). You decide with one call whether to flag the tender as collusive. If you flag it, the lowest valid bid is discarded and the next lowest valid bid wins. You cannot read the colluders' private messages.
